> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# The Scion Standard

The Scion Standard is a small set of rules for how a Unity game is organized so that Scion, people and agents can
extend it safely. Its five principles say where rules live and how they change; its six layers (Core, Presentation,
Grafts, Adapters, Trials, Tests) say what may depend on what. Analyzers SCN001 to SCN005, `doctor` and the scaffolds
of `scion new` enforce it; nothing in it is required to use grafts or trials, but every rule you follow makes the
adapter thinner and unlocks more of Scion.

## How it works

### Five principles

1. **Rules are explicit in the core.** Plain C#, deterministic, integer math, extended by registration
   (`RuleModifier<T>`), never by IL weaving.
2. **Weaving happens only in presentation.** Grafts are visual; deleting the grafts folder still compiles and plays
   the same.
3. **Shallow inheritance, content as data.** A new enemy or ability is a data row plus a registered strategy, not a
   subclass tree.
4. **Commands go down, events come up.** Presentation sends commands to the core and reacts to its events; the
   methods that react are the anchors.
5. **Types, analyzers and `doctor` enforce the standard**, not long text files. Context files alone help little and
   cost tokens on every request.

### Six layers

| Layer | Contains | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| Core | Rules, state, commands, events, rule tunables, the `ISimulation` | nothing of Unity |
| Presentation | Views, HUD, camera, audio, the `Fx` sink | Core |
| Grafts | `[Before]`/`[After]` methods, presentation tunables | Presentation, Core (read only) |
| Adapters | `TrialAdapter<T>`, network and input ports | Core, Presentation |
| Trials | Recipes, checks, specs | Adapters, Core |
| Tests | `dotnet test` projects, completeness tests | anything |

The dependency rule: arrows point down the table and never back up. Nothing depends on Grafts (SCN110); the Core
depends on nothing of Unity (an assembly with `noEngineReferences: true`).

### In Orchard

| Layer | Orchard |
|---|---|
| Core | `Orchard.Core`: `BattleState`, `Command`, `DamageCalc`, `BackstabBonus : RuleModifier<DamageCalc>` |
| Presentation | `Orchard.Runtime`: `HitPresenter`, `Hud`, `CameraRig`, `DamageNumbers`, `OrchardFxSink` |
| Grafts | `Assets/Orchard/Grafts`: `HitFlash`, `CritShake`, `DamageNumberPop`, `TurnBanner` |
| Adapters | `OrchardAdapter`, `OrchardMatchCapture` |
| Trials | `Orchard.Trials`: `SlashHit`, `CoopTurn`, `HudStates`; `Trials/Specs` |
| Tests | `Tests/Orchard.Core.Tests`, `Tests/Orchard.Grafts.Tests` |

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Core | The rules assembly, listed in `analyzers.rule_assemblies`. |
| Rule code | Code in the core; follows SCN001, SCN002 and SCN004. |
| Primitive | One of the standard's building blocks ([Primitives](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/primitives/)). |
| Exemplar | A small, compiled, tested example in the project that agents copy. |
| Completeness test | A test that every enum value has a handler, every enemy a presentation. |

## Guarantees and limits

- Following the standard is gradual: each rule stands alone, and `doctor` reports the adoption level.
- The analyzers only report on assemblies you list; third-party code is never checked.
- Deviations are allowed with a justification, through the normal Roslyn suppression.

## See also

# Rules R1-R8

Each rule below has a statement, the reason, an example from Orchard and how Scion checks it. Rules are numbered for
reference in reviews and in agent instructions ("this breaks R3"). Analyzer ids are in
[SCN001-SCN005](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/standard/).

## R1 Inherit one level from a Scion base, sealed

**Why.** The base controls the flow (Template Method), so subclasses cannot get it wrong, and `sealed` lets IL2CPP
devirtualize calls.

```csharp
public sealed class OrchardAdapter : TrialAdapter<OrchardRecipe> { /* ... */ }
public sealed class BackstabBonus : RuleModifier<DamageCalc> { /* ... */ }
public sealed class HudStates : StaticTrial<HudState> { /* ... */ }
```

**Enforced by** SCN001 (not sealed) and SCN002 (more than one level) in rule code.

## R2 Anchors take values, not services

**Why.** An anchor method whose parameters are plain values (`HitEvent`, `int turn`) gives grafts everything they
need without reaching into services, and keeps grafts testable with `new Call<T>(...)`.

```csharp
public float Play(HitEvent e)   // HitEvent is a readonly struct: attacker, target, amount, crit
```

**Enforced by** review and the exemplars; `anchor show` prints the signature grafts bind to.

## R3 Rules that change numbers are RuleModifier

**Why.** A rule change registered explicitly with a stage, a priority and integers is visible, ordered and the same
on every peer. A graft that changed it would vanish outside Unity.

```csharp
public sealed class BackstabBonus : RuleModifier<DamageCalc>
{
    public override Stage Stage => Stage.Mul;
    public override int Priority => 10;
    public override void Apply(ref DamageCalc c) { if (c.FromBehind) c.MulPermille += 500; }
}
```

**Enforced by** SCN003 (a graft writes rule state), SCN004 (`float` in rule code: use `int` or permille so every
machine computes the same result) and the hash A/B run.

## R4 New content is a Type Object plus a strategy by enum

**Why.** A new ability is a data row and one case in a strategy, so completeness can be tested: every enum value has
a handler.

```csharp
public enum AbilityEffect { Damage, Heal, Push }
public static int Resolve(AbilityEffect e, ref DamageCalc c) => e switch
{
    AbilityEffect.Damage => Damage.Apply(ref c),
    AbilityEffect.Heal => Heal.Apply(ref c),
    AbilityEffect.Push => Push.Apply(ref c),
    _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(e)),
};
```

**Enforced by** completeness tests generated by `scion new effect`.

## R5 Interfaces only for context and optional capabilities

**Why.** Interfaces such as `ISaveable` or `IMirrorable` say what the state can do; using them for everything adds
indirection without value. Serialized types avoid `record` and `init`, which Unity's serializer does not support.

**Enforced by** review and `doctor`'s capability report.

## R6 Every mutation is a Command

**Why.** Commands can be logged, replayed, captured with F9, forked in the multiverse and sent over the network.
Event dispatch is a `switch` calling named methods, and those methods become anchors.

```csharp
battle.Issue(Command.Ability("slash", attacker: 0, target: 1));
```

**Enforced by** level 3 requirements: `ISimulation.Apply(command)` is the only way to change state.

## R7 The adapter is a Template Method

**Why.** One public, non-virtual entry point per job (build state, apply a command, hash) keeps adapters small and
the same across games.

**Enforced by** `TrialAdapter<TRecipe>` and the skeleton `diagnose --adapter` writes.

## R8 Helpers by composition

**Why.** A thin facade object (`Fx`) gives every graft the same verbs without a fat base class. Extension methods
only on struct contexts.

**Enforced by** the `Fx` facade and the exemplars.

# Primitives

A primitive is a building block with one job. Choosing the right one is most of following the standard: a number
that changes a rule is a `RuleModifier<T>`, a sound on a hit is a graft, a number someone will tune is a
`[Tunable]`. This page lists each primitive, when to use it and where it is documented.

## Table

| Primitive | Use it for | Never for | Docs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[Anchor(Id, Doc)]` | Stable, documented presentation moments agents should find first. | Rule methods. | [Anchors](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/anchors/) |
| Graft (`[Before]`/`[After]`) | Juice, sound, camera, HUD, telemetry, tutorial hints. | Changing a rule. | [Write a graft](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/write/) |
| `RuleModifier<T>` + `Stage` | Any rule that changes a number (damage, range, cost). | Presentation. | [Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/) |
| Strategy by enum | Effects, AI choices, presentation per effect. | Open-ended plugins. | [Rules R1-R8](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/rules/) |
| Type Object | Immutable definitions: abilities, units, rooms (data rows, or a ScriptableObject compiled to a table). | State that changes during a match. | [Rules R1-R8](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/rules/) |
| `[Tunable(min, max)]` | A number someone tunes; on rule fields, it enters the lobby hash. | Constants nobody tunes. | [Tunables and presets](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/tunables/) |
| `[Probe("key")]` | A rule value recorded in trials. | Per-frame values (use a sensor). | [Telemetry, probes and sensors](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/telemetry/) |
| Cue | A visual triggered by an event, one-shot or added and removed (a burning aura). | Logic. | below |
| Adapter | The game's port: trials, network, input. | Game rules. | [Write an adapter](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/adapters/) |
| Exemplar | A small compiled, tested example per primitive for agents to copy. | Documentation prose. | below |

## Stages of a rule modifier

| Stage | Order | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `Stage.Base` | 1 | Set the base value from data. |
| `Stage.Add` | 2 | Flat bonuses. |
| `Stage.Mul` | 3 | Multipliers in permille (`MulPermille += 500` is +50 %). |
| `Stage.Clamp` | 4 | Minimums, maximums, immunities. |
| `Stage.Final` | 5 | Last-word effects (shields that absorb). |

Within a stage, `Priority` orders modifiers (lower first), then the type's full name.

## Cues

A cue is a pattern, not a type: a presentation method that reacts to one core event, named after it, and therefore
an anchor.

```csharp
public sealed class StatusCues : MonoBehaviour
{
    public void OnBurnAdded(int unit) => Auras.Add(unit, "burn");
    public void OnBurnRemoved(int unit) => Auras.Remove(unit, "burn");
}
```

Grafts on `OnBurnAdded` add sound or shake without touching the status system.

## Exemplars

`Assets/Orchard/Exemplars/` holds one file per primitive (`ExemplarGraft.cs`, `ExemplarModifier.cs`,
`ExemplarRecipe.cs`...), compiled with the project and covered by a test. `scion new` copies from them, and the
project index points agents to them.

## See also

- [Enforcement](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/enforcement/)

# Enforcement

The standard is enforced by tools, not by long text: Roslyn analyzers (SCN001 to SCN005, plus SCN003 and SCN110 for
grafts) report in the IDE and in Unity, scoped to the assemblies you list in `ScionSettings.json`; `doctor` reports
the adoption level and what is missing; `scion new` scaffolds code that already passes; completeness tests catch
missing handlers. This guide sets them up.

## When to use

- When adopting the standard in a project: set the scope first, then fix warnings gradually.
- When reviewing agent changes: the analyzers and tests catch most deviations before review.

## Steps

### 1. Scope the analyzers

`ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json`:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"analyzers":{"rule_assemblies":["Orchard.Core"],"rule_types":["Unity.Netcode.*"],"graft_paths":["Assets/Orchard/Grafts/","../scion/grafts/"]}}
```

Only the assemblies in `rule_assemblies` get SCN001, SCN002, SCN004 and SCN005. Recompile after editing.

### 2. Scaffold new code

```sh
dotnet scion new feature Burn
dotnet scion new effect Push
dotnet scion new graft BurnAuraSound --after Orchard.Presentation.StatusCues.OnBurnAdded
dotnet scion new trial BurnTicks
```

Each command writes code that compiles and passes `doctor`, copied from the project's exemplars: a feature gets its
modifier, its data row and a recipe; an effect gets its enum case, its strategy and a completeness test entry.

### 3. Check the project

```sh
dotnet scion doctor --level 3
```

## Reference

### Analyzers

| Id | Severity | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| SCN001 | warning | A class in rule code is not sealed (R1). |
| SCN002 | warning | A class in rule code inherits more than one level (R1). |
| SCN003 | error | A graft writes rule state (R3). |
| SCN004 | warning | `float` in rule code (R3). |
| SCN005 | warning | A numeric `[Tunable]` without a range. |
| SCN110 | error | Game code calls a graft. |

The analyzers ship in the package (`Scion.Analyzers`, labeled `RoslynAnalyzer`), so Unity and IDEs that read Unity's
generated projects run them. For `dotnet build` outside Unity, add the `Scion.Testing` package, which carries them.

### Suppressing a deviation

```csharp
[SuppressMessage("Scion", "SCN002", Justification = "Netcode requires NetworkBehaviour as the base")]
public sealed class TurnSync : TurnSyncBase { }
```

or `#pragma warning disable SCN004` around the lines. `doctor` lists every suppression with its justification.

### Completeness tests

`scion new effect` adds the effect to `Tests/Orchard.Core.Tests/Completeness.cs`:

```csharp
[Fact]
public void Every_effect_has_a_handler()
{
    foreach (AbilityEffect e in Enum.GetValues(typeof(AbilityEffect)))
        Assert.True(Effects.Handles(e), $"{e} has no handler");
}
```

Other completeness tests in the template: every unit kind has a presentation, every status has cues, every rule
tunable has a range.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN001`-`SCN005` | compile warning or error | See the table above. | Follow the hint, or suppress with a justification. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | `scion new` with an unknown kind. | Use `feature`, `effect`, `graft` or `trial`. |

## Examples

### Fail CI on standard warnings in the core

```sh
dotnet build Trials/Specs/Orchard.Specs.csproj -warnaserror:SCN001,SCN002,SCN004,SCN005
```

### Preview a scaffold

```sh
dotnet scion new feature Burn --dry-run
```
